title: Adaptive reservoir-based batcher with KV prefetch coalescing for heterogeneous turn lengths
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
We operate a continuous-batching runtime that services mixed prompt/response workloads (chatty turns where prompts are short and responses vary widely). Current scheduler heuristics depend on static length buckets and earliest-deadline-first slot assignment which underutilizes GPU occupancy for heterogeneous dialogues and causes frequent KV cache churn for long-turn requests.

Goal:
Design and implement an adaptive reservoir-based slot allocator that: (1) preserves low tail latency for short-turn interactive requests, (2) increases packing density for medium/long responses via temporal coalescing, and (3) reduces KV cache thrash by coalescing prefetch windows and introducing a soft-tenure watermark for hot KV residency.

Approach:
- Reservoir sampler for incoming slots: maintain per-GPU reservoirs stratified by recent turn-horizon statistics (short/medium/long) and use proportional admission to avoid starvation of short turns while creating larger packing cohorts for medium/long turns.
- Temporal coalescing window: allow the scheduler to extend a small, configurable time budget (coalesce_ms) to wait for compatible turns that improve packing, with adaptive decay based on observed p95 latency drift.
- KV prefetch coalescing: group nearby slots targeting the same model/version into a single KV read batch when within the same coalescing window, reducing duplicate prefetches and improving KV cache locality.
- Soft-tenure watermarking: mark recently prefetched KV shards as "soft-hot" and prevent eviction until a configured soft-tenure or until memory pressure requires compaction; provide a fast-path for eviction of truly cold shards.
- Slab packing and thin-slicing: coordinate with GPU slab allocator to place coalesced batches into contiguous slab spans, reducing fragmentation.
- Per-model profile tuning: keep profile hints (avg sequence length, kv-residency preference) to bias reservoir admission and coalescing threshold.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end p95 generation latency for short-turn requests increases by <= 8ms compared to baseline under production mixed workload (95th percentile target unchanged or better).
- Average GPU token throughput increases 6-12% in mixed traffic synthetic bench.
- KV prefetch duplicate reads reduced by >= 30% for a representative 48-hour trace.
- KV cache eviction churn (measured as number of re-prefetches per shard per hour) reduced by >= 20%.
- Canary rollout path implemented with config flags to disable reservoir admission and to tune coalesce_ms at runtime.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Coalescing window could increase tail latency if mis-tuned. Mitigation: adaptive decay and runtime guard rails that disable coalescing when p95 exceeds threshold; canary filter to sample users.
- Risk: Soft-tenure increases memory pressure leading to OOM. Mitigation: conservative default soft-tenure, integrated GPU slab compaction trigger, and early-fallback to hard eviction under memory emergency.
- Risk: Increased scheduler complexity may impact scheduler CPU utilization. Mitigation: keep admission/eviction operations O(1) amortized via reservoir sampling and maintain per-GPU local metadata to avoid global locks.

Test plan:
- Microbench: synthetic traces with controlled short/medium/long mix; compare throughput, p50/p95/p99 latencies, KV prefetch counts, eviction churn.
- Replay bench: 48hr production traffic replay to validate duplicate prefetch reduction and memory behavior.
- Canary: deploy to 5% of serving capacity for 72h with metrics dashboard and auto-roll-back thresholds.
- Load test: spike and gradual ramp tests to validate compaction and emergency eviction behavior.

Rollout and observability:
- Feature flag: runtime.reservoir_coalescing (boolean) and runtime.coalesce_ms (int) per-route and per-model.
- Metrics: scheduler_coalesced_batches_total, kv_prefetch_dedup_ratio, gpu_slab_fragmentation_ratio, kv_eviction_churn_per_hour, generation_p95_short_turns.
- Logs: structured events when soft-tenure eviction occurs and when coalescing window triggers.

Implementation notes:
- Prefer Rust code path in scheduler for lower-latency admission logic; prototype in python for algorithm verification.
- Reuse existing KV prefetch layer but add a coalescing key (model, version, shard_range) to deduplicate reads.
- Coordinate with infra team for GPU slab allocator hooks (compact_span API).

updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created. Initial spike goals and acceptance criteria documented.
2026-03-02: Algorithm spike completed (python prototype). Reservoir admission reduces slot starvation in playground trace. Baseline p95 impact measured small (+3ms).

2026-03-04: Bench harness: synthetic mix (60% short, 30% medium, 10% long) shows +9% throughput with naive coalescing but p95 drifted +12ms. Added adaptive decay heuristic to coalesce_ms based on realtime p95 signal.
2026-03-06: Design review with KV team — agreed on coalescing key structure and soft-tenure semantics. Concurrency model: per-GPU local metadata to avoid global locking.
2026-03-08: Started Rust implementation of scheduler admission and coalescing; opened RFC for slab compact_span hook. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4281
2026-03-10: Integrated KV dedupe in bench harness. Duplicate prefetch count down ~35% in replayed 24h segment. Preparing canary plan and dashboard tiles.
notes: Coordinate with Observability (Samantha Lee) to add generation_p95_short_turns metric before canary.
Estimate includes time for benching, implementation, and a single canary roll-out cycle.
If soft-tenure shows regression in memory-critical regions, we will iterate with a smaller default and enable per-customer overrides for Dedicated clusters.
